 Andhra Pradesh Bay of Bengal system likely to become cyclone by November 16; rain alert for Andhra Pradesh
 Subhransu Satpathy 15 Nov 2026 7:16 AM Share this: HYDERABAD: The India Meteorological Department ( IMD ) has issued an alert over a developing weather system in the Southeast Bay of Bengal. The system is likely to intensify into a depression before developing into a cyclonic storm by the evening of November 16, 2026.
 According to the IMD, a well-marked low-pressure area formed over the Southeast Bay of Bengal on November 14. It is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression within the next 24 hours. 
 The system is then expected to move north-northwestwards. It could develop into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal.

 The IMD’s Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC), New Delhi, has also indicated the possibility of further intensification. Its November 14 outlook suggests that the system could strengthen into a deep depression on November 16. It may then develop into a cyclonic storm. The forecast also indicates the possibility of a severe cyclonic storm by November 18.
 The system was located near latitude 7.3°N and longitude 87.8°E at 8:30 am IST on November 14. Its associated cyclonic circulation extended up to 7.6 km above mean sea level. 
 Wind speed and sea conditions
 The IMD expects maximum sustained wind speeds of 40–50 kmph when the system develops into a depression on November 15. Wind speeds could increase to 60–70 kmph as it intensifies into a cyclonic storm on November 16.
 The RSMC outlook indicates a further increase by November 18. Wind speeds could reach 75–85 kmph, with gusts of up to 95 kmph, if the system strengthens as forecast.
 The IMD has also reported cyclonic winds of 20–25 knots, with gusts of up to 30 knots, over parts of the Southeast Bay of Bengal and South Andaman Sea.
 Sea conditions could remain moderate to rough. Some areas may experience very rough conditions.
 Fishermen and coastal communities advised to remain alert
 The IMD has advised fishermen, coastal residents and marine operators to monitor official weather bulletins. They should also follow instructions from local authorities and avoid venturing into areas covered by warnings.
 The system’s movement and intensity may change with subsequent updates. Residents should rely on official IMD advisories rather than unverified social media reports.
 Andhra Pradesh rainfall forecast; Telangana impact limited
 The developing weather system could influence rainfall across Andhra Pradesh over the coming days.
 According to the IMD’s November 14 forecast, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema may receive isolated to scattered rainfall between November 14 and 19.
 The IMD has also forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 18 and 19.
 However, the forecast does not indicate a significant direct impact on Telangana at this stage. Hyderabad and other parts of the state are not currently under a specific cyclone-related warning in the information cited here.
 The IMD continues to monitor the system. Its subsequent bulletins will provide greater clarity on the cyclone’s track, intensity and possible impact along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
